answer: A Sybil defense should treat identity as a living atlas, not a badge. Each account starts with a bare kernel of trust that grows only through dawn-patrol participation: irregular, unannounced check-ins spread across days, each requiring a small, fresh task that cannot be scripted in advance. One operator running many accounts hits a scheduling wall — the check-ins never align, so tending a farm means being awake at every dawn, forever. Genuine users build a scattered, idiosyncratic atlas of activity that is costly to fake in bulk but cheap to live. Sybils cluster in time; humans scatter.
